clue.text: Rough passage, it's said?

indicators.note: what is said is heard rather than read, so the word for passage is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a course is a passage or route, and it sounds exactly like the word wanted

explanation.surface: Someone warns of a rough crossing or a stormy stretch of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse and rough are synonyms describing a texture that is not smooth.

clue.text: Great lover with sex appeal certainly not into wine

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

blocks.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
SA is the abbreviation for sex appeal
an emphatic refusal

explanation.surface: A legendary seducer, oozing charm, firmly declines a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Cava is a Spanish sparkling wine; SA for sex appeal is a crossword abbreviation worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Casanova was an eighteenth-century Venetian famous for his seductions, so his name means a womaniser.

clue.text: Expect there's a load to listen to?

indicators.note: something to listen to is heard, so the phrase is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a load is a weight, and the two words run together sound like the answer

explanation.surface: Someone anticipates a heavy burden, or a big pile of music to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to wait for it in anticipation, a synonym of expect.

clue.text: Set tailors up on wet land

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: a tailor fits a garment to a customer
a fen is low marshy ground, as in eastern England

explanation.surface: Tailors are being set up to work on marshland.
explanation.definitionFit: To set is to harden or become firm, as jelly or concrete does, which is what stiffen means.

clue.text: Not this cold, hot layer of straw, say?

blocks.note: the pointing word that is the alternative to this
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between materials rejects one option for a warm covering of straw.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is the roofing of straw or reed laid in a thick covering, so a straw layer is an example.

clue.text: So mad having trodden on nail, perhaps?

blocks.note: first meaning: the intensifier in the idiom for furious
second meaning: what you do on one foot after a painful step

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hopping mad' means very angry, so the word stands in for 'so' before mad; a nail in the foot makes you jump about on the other one.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopping is the idiomatic intensifier in hopping mad, and also literally jumping on one foot in pain.

clue.text: A great new haunt where refreshments served outdoors

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
a den is a favourite hangout

explanation.surface: A fine new spot to hang out where food and drinks are served in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea garden is an outdoor café area where tea and snacks are served, so the description defines it.

clue.text: Unhappy after short vacation in cave

blocks.note: HOL is a shortening of holiday, the British word for a vacation
feeling low means feeling down

explanation.surface: Someone feels gloomy after a brief holiday spent in a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the word for unhappy behind the short holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow is a cavity or hole, and a cave is a hollow in rock.

clue.text: Daydreaming, put first of Cornish pasties in a stew

indicators.note: the first of a word means only its opening letter is kept
something in a stew is in a muddle, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the opening letter of Cornish
taken as written, to be mixed with the letter before it

explanation.surface: A distracted cook drifts off while putting Cornish pasties into a stew.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapist describes fantasy that lets one flee reality, much as idle daydreaming does; both are adjectives here.

clue.text: Ailing puss, I repeat, delicate thing

indicators.note: something ailing is unwell and out of order, so the following letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone insists, again, that their sick cat is a fragile creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue paper is very thin, fragile paper used for wrapping, so it is a delicate thing.

clue.text: Smooth and tough Arctic explorer saving lives, originally

indicators.note: originally points to the start of a word, so only its first letter is used
saving means keeping something safe inside, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: Robert Peary, the American explorer who claimed to reach the North Pole
the first letter of lives

explanation.surface: A rugged polar explorer is praised for rescuing people in the ice.
explanation.walkthrough: The L goes inside PEARY to give PEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pearly has the lustrous, even sheen of a pearl, so it is glossy and smooth.

clue.text: Wading bird that may be on reef?

blocks.note: first meaning: a sandpiper of shores and estuaries
second meaning: a tie in rope, of which the reef type is one

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a shorebird perched on a coral reef, but reef is the name of a sailor's tie.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird of the sandpiper family shares its name with a fastening in rope, and a reef one is a common example.

clue.text: Decorative accessory turning into a scarf

indicators.note: turning means changing form or direction, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A fashion item is being refashioned into a scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' reads as part of 'turning into', but its letters belong to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascinator is a small ornamental headpiece worn at weddings and races, a piece of decorative headwear.

clue.text: Devouring rubbish including last scrap of meal, journalist ate too much

indicators.note: rubbish means worthless junk, so the word before it is treated as scrambled
the last scrap of a word is its closing letter alone

blocks.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
the final letter of meal, added to the jumble
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A greedy reporter scoffs everything, even the scraps, and eats far too much.
explanation.definitionFit: To overindulge is to have more food or drink than is good for you, so its past tense matches gorged.

clue.text: Bird breeds with rat, remarkably

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something done in an unusual way, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unlikely tale of a bird interbreeding with a rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: Redbreast is an old name for the robin, so it is a particular bird.

clue.text: Big blows in general — lawyers' terms?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general of the American Civil War
gales are strong winds

explanation.surface: Massive punches thrown in a general's direction, described in legal jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in general' reads as 'generally', but the general is a specific person.
explanation.definitionFit: Legalese is the jargon-heavy language of legal documents, the vocabulary lawyers use.

clue.text: Upset as given the sack, it's implied?

blocks.note: surface reading: let down by how things turned out

blocks.clueFragment: as given the sack, it's implied?
blocks.note: setter's reading: split the word as DIS plus a word for given a post, so un-hired, which is what being sacked is

explanation.walkthrough: Read as dis- plus appointed, the word suggests being removed from a job; the real meaning is simply let down.
explanation.definitionFit: Disappointed means saddened by a failed hope, which is a common sense of upset as an adjective.

clue.text: Observe servant providing quantity of dripping?

blocks.note: to observe is to see
a page is a young attendant

explanation.surface: A servant is watched handing over a measure of meat fat.
explanation.walkthrough: Dripping is British cooking fat from roast meat, which misleads; here it means leaking liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is the amount of liquid that leaks slowly through, so a quantity that has dripped.

clue.text: Boaters in Sanremo at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means being confused, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: taken as written; Sanremo is an Italian Riviera resort

explanation.surface: Boating people are out on the water off an Italian seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Boaters looks like the straw hats; it means people in boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Oarsmen row boats, so they are people who go boating.

clue.text: Musical about Genesis etc lifting agent?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the musical goes round the other piece

blocks.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
Genesis and the books after it make up the Old Testament, OT

explanation.surface: A stage show about Genesis and other works boosts someone's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis looks like the rock band; here it is the first book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot air rises, so it is what lifts a balloon; the question mark flags the less obvious sense.

clue.text: Opener: cricketer who's gloved bouncer, say?

blocks.note: a door is something that opens
the wicketkeeper is the cricket fielder who wears gloves

explanation.surface: A cricket line-up: the opening batsman, the gloved wicketkeeper, and a short fast ball called a bouncer.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bouncer is a short-pitched fast ball, but here it is a nightclub doorman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouncer guards the entrance of a club, which is one example of someone who keeps a door.

clue.text: Mend part of shoe, did you say?

indicators.note: asking what someone said points to the sound of the word, not its spelling

blocks.note: the raised back of a shoe, which sounds identical to the answer

explanation.surface: A cobbler is asked to repair a section of a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: To heal is to make well again, a synonym of mend when said of wounds or rifts.

clue.text: One in Panama, say, heading for idyllic island nation

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the headwear
the heading of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a Panama is a straw hat
the Roman numeral for one
the first letter of idyllic

explanation.surface: A traveller in Panama sets off for an idyllic Caribbean island country.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside HA-T, then the initial of idyllic follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is a Caribbean country on the island of Hispaniola, so it is an island nation.

clue.text: Two family members together soon enough

blocks.note: MA is a familiar name for mother
NANA is a familiar name for grandmother

explanation.surface: Two relatives will be coming along before too long.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces come from the same phrase: the two members are mother and grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: Mañana is Spanish for tomorrow, used in English for an easygoing promise of some later time.

clue.text: Around New England state, communist stayed

indicators.note: Around means surrounding, so one word goes outside another

blocks.note: red is the colour of communism
Maine is the north-eastern state in New England

explanation.surface: A communist settled in a New England state and stayed put.
explanation.definitionFit: Remained and stayed are synonyms, both past tense verbs for staying in place.

clue.text: Preferably pretty

blocks.note: first meaning: as in I would sooner do that
second meaning: fairly or somewhat, as in pretty good

explanation.walkthrough: 'pretty' looks like an adjective meaning attractive, but it is the adverb meaning fairly.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb expresses preference in one use and moderate degree in another, matching both words.

clue.text: Where log may be doing very well

blocks.note: first meaning: a log burns in the grate
second meaning: performing brilliantly, as a player in form

explanation.walkthrough: The literal phrase locates burning wood; the idiom describes someone in hot form.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally places a log in flames and idiomatically means performing excellently or on a hot streak.
